title: Fast and Synchronous Crash Consistency with Metadata Write-Once File System
problem: Traditional file systems require complex recovery procedures and journaling to ensure crash consistency; write-once approach could simplify this
motivation: Reliable storage is critical for AI training checkpoints and model artifacts; simpler crash consistency mechanisms reduce complexity and potential bugs
method: Instead of modifying file metadata in place, the system writes new versions to fresh disk locations, never overwriting the old data. This means a crash can only leave you with the previous complete version or the new complete version—never a partially written, corrupted mixture. The system waits for each write to physically reach disk before confirming it's done (synchronous writes), ensuring consistency without traditional journaling (backup logs used for recovery).
key_novelty: This file system achieves synchronous crash consistency for file metadata by using a write-once approach (writing metadata to new locations instead of overwriting it), eliminating the need for traditional recovery journals.
contributions: Simplified consistency model vs traditional journaling
limitations: Title-only paper; performance overhead/benefits not quantified; write amplification and wear concerns not addressed
